description: Resize, crop, rotate, flip, compress (to a file size with target_bytes), convert (jpeg, png, webp, avif), strip EXIF and GPS metadata from, and watermark (text, logo or both) one image or a zip of up to 50 images (up to 500 files per zip; files that are not supported images are skipped and listed). Crops are in pixels by default; for a zip of different sizes use crop_unit "percent" or crop_aspect, which are worked out per image. Give exactly one source: file_id (from create_upload), url (public https) or data_base64 (up to 3 MB inline; use create_upload, up to 100 MB, or url above that). One image in returns one image; a zip returns a zip. AVIF output is scaled down to fit 1,200 px on the longest side and WebP output to 36 megapixels. Returns a 24-hour download_url with the size and format of every output, and for each output the kinds of metadata found in the input and left in the output (location, date, camera, serial number, ...) and whether the colour profile was kept; kinds only, never the values. keep_date and keep_copyright write back the EXIF date taken and copyright after stripping. Large zips can take up to a minute; use a client timeout of at least 120 s. Free. Daily quotas are counted per caller in output megapixels; see start.md.

background.description: JPEG only: colour under transparent areas, #rrggbb

crop_aspect.description: Instead of the four crop fields: the largest centered crop of this width:height ratio, per image

crop_height.description: Crop: height (px, or % of the height with crop_unit percent)

crop_left.description: Crop: left edge (px, or % of the width with crop_unit percent)

crop_top.description: Crop: top edge (px, or % of the height with crop_unit percent)

crop_unit.description: Unit of the four crop fields: px (whole pixels) or percent (0-100 of each image, so a zip of different sizes gets the same part of every image)

crop_width.description: Crop: width (px, or % of the width with crop_unit percent)

data_base64.description: Base64 bytes of an image or zip, up to 3 MB decoded; use create_upload (up to 100 MB) or url above that

file_id.description: Image or zip file (up to 25 MB on this page)

filename.description: Name for the output when the source has none

fit.description: How to fit into width x height: scale-down never enlarges; cover fills and crops; pad adds borders

flip.description: Flip: h = horizontal, v = vertical, hv = both

format.description: Output format (keep turns HEIC into JPEG and GIF into PNG)

keep_copyright.description: With strip_metadata: keep the EXIF Copyright tag. XMP and IPTC rights are not kept

keep_date.description: With strip_metadata: keep the EXIF date taken (DateTimeOriginal and DateTimeDigitized, with their time zone and fraction of a second) so photos still sort by date. A date and time taken found only in XMP or PNG text is written as the EXIF DateTimeOriginal; IPTC dates are not kept

max_side.description: Instead of width and height: the longest side in pixels, per image, so portrait and landscape images both get it on their long edge. Never enlarges unless fit is contain

quality.description: Quality 1-100 for JPEG, WebP and AVIF; lower is smaller. Ignored with target_bytes

resize_unit.description: Unit of width and height: px, or percent (1-1000) of each image's own size, so a zip of different sizes is scaled alike. Over 100 enlarges only with fit contain

strip_metadata.description: Remove EXIF, GPS location and camera data

target_bytes.description: Instead of quality: the most bytes each output may have (10,000-50,000,000; 1 MB = 1,000,000), for upload forms with a size limit. Uses the highest quality from 45 to 92 that fits; if even 45 is too big, the image is scaled down too. Each item then reports the quality used, and over_target when it could not get under

url.description: Or a public https URL of an image or zip

watermark_image.description: Logo for the watermark, with or instead of watermark_text: a file_id from create_upload, a public https url, or data:image/png;base64,... (up to 1 MB inline; an inline image and logo share the 3 MB inline limit). PNG with transparency is best; WebP and JPEG work. Up to 2 MB and 2048 px on the longest side; rasterise SVG to PNG first. With text, the logo sits left of the text and both are placed as one

watermark_image_size.description: Logo width, % of each image's width (2-50). Default 15

watermark_position.description: Watermark position; custom places the centre of the text at watermark_x, watermark_y

watermark_size.description: Watermark font size: px (8-400, whole numbers) or, with watermark_size_unit percent, % of each image's width (0.5-20, giving 12-1000 px). Default 4% of the width

watermark_size_unit.description: Unit of watermark_size: px, or percent of each image's width (so a zip of different sizes gets the same relative size)

watermark_x.description: With watermark_position custom: the centre of the text, % of each image's width from the left (0-100)

watermark_y.description: With watermark_position custom: the centre of the text, % of each image's height from the top (0-100)

name: process_images

metadata.description: The kinds of metadata found in the input and left in the output; never the values

color_profile.description: kept: the input's colour profile is in the output; converted_to_srgb: the profile was not kept and the encoder converted the colours to sRGB; none: the input had none; unknown: the input could not be read

found.description: Kinds of metadata in the input, never their values; null when not readable

readable.description: Whether the input's metadata could be read (false for GIF and damaged headers)

remaining.description: Kinds of metadata still in the output: [] after strip_metadata, or only date and copyright with keep_date and keep_copyright; null when the output could not be read
